svg.title: aero-safe-rl architecture
svg.desc: Left: Isaac Lab trains the recovery policy on up to 32,768 parallel drones, flying PX4's x500 under a PyTorch port of PX4's controller. Middle: the two conda environments exchange only files (observation/action spec, normalisation stats, policy checkpoint, fault fixture, fitted detector simulator). Right: the PX4-in-the-loop stack (Gazebo, stock PX4, ROS 2, AI fault detector, recovery policy) produces every reported number. The policy only sends high-level commands, never motor commands.
svg.text: aero-safe-rl · train in the gym, sit the exam in PX4
16 of 16 agreement checks with PX4 pass
noise + lag fitted to the real detector
32,768 drones crash so one doesn't have to
slow down · divert · land — never a motor command
Each drone gets its own Gazebo server, its own clock, its own identity file.
Nobody shares a world. Nobody special-cases instance 0.
PX4 flies the drone. We're the backseat navigator.
We say “slow down”, “go home”, “land”. We never grab the stick.
the policy never sees the true fault · Isaac numbers are for training curves only · PX4 numbers go in the paper
